newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek shares slide in narrow trade, inflation eases.
newsitem.headline: Greek shares slide in narrow trade, inflation eases.

text.p: Greek equities shrugged off a slightly improved August inflation figure and closed lower in narrow trade after climbing early in the session.
Market watchers said the benchmark share index was likely to hover around 930 points until election time September 22.

"Stocks will continue to consolidate and hover around 930 points, building a base at this level until the elections. Polls out so far show Pasok is leading the race but there is a large amount of undecided voters," said fund manager Evangelos Memmos at Delphi Mutual Funds.
He said falling interest rates favoured bank shares which were forming a base for a further rally but expected construction shares to correct in the near term on profit taking.
Memmos liked Athens Medical Center, Metka and Elmec Sport, forecasting good returns on sound fundamentals for these companies.

"As we move closer to the elections on September 22 the market will tend to reflect polls showing which party is ahead among voter preferences but not much will change until after the outcome," Memmos said.

The Athens general share index closed 0.21 percent, or 1.97 points lower at 932.34 from Wednesday's 934.31 close after opening at 933.50 points. Turnover eased to 6.72 billion drachmas on volume of 4.01 million shares.
In line with market expectations, August CPI inflation slowed to 8.5 percent year-on-year from 8.6 percent in July, the National Statistics Service (NSS) said.
Bankers and economists had forecast August inflation would ease to 8.5 percent year-on-year in an earlier Reuters informal poll.
Greece will hold early elections September 22.
